checks_run.procedure: Live stack on a fresh PostgreSQL 16 database: migrate twice, seed the SYNTHETIC dev users, then start the API (AUTH_MODE=dev) and the worker as separate processes. The HTTP probe (01a) re-runs the round-1 domain checks: the close rule (draft, active and on_hold to closed are refused 422 with the record and version unchanged; a combined close plus rename is refused atomically; the message names neither DG7 nor an approval); defaults Asia/Riyadh and SAR, with modular entry and configurable timezone and currency; If-Match 428 and 409/412; audit only for successful mutations; scoped access (TL 404 out of scope, admin sees no business records, auditor read-only, CSRF 403); cursor pagination (complete walk, cursor bound to sort, tamper and limit rejected); provisional branding tokens; and locale preferences. Round-2 additions: BU re-parent cycle (A>B>C, then A under C and A under A are refused 422 business_unit.cycle and A is unchanged); an org-scope ADM_TECH moves a BU to the top and back; BU PATCH without If-Match gives 428; destination authorization (a user with ADM_TECH on Y only gets 403 moving Y under X or under SYN-FIN, can still rename Y, gets 200 once also granted X, and gets 403 moving Y to the top level, where the destination is the organization); a direct UPDATE as mth_app is refused by the 0009 trigger; denials are audited; the closure view has no self-cycles. Then the worker stop test
checks_run.environment: Node v22.22.2, PostgreSQL 16.13 disposable cluster on 127.0.0.1:54393, API on :3000, worker as a separate process, synthetic data only
checks_run.expected: every probe check PASS; the DB guard refuses the cycle; the API survives the worker stop
checks_run.actual: API probe SUMMARY pass=49 fail=0. Cycle refusal: 422 {code: business_unit.cycle}. Destination-authz refusals: 403 forbidden, with 5 authorization.denied audit events, the latest naming 'PATCH /api/v1/business-units/:businessUnitId requires business_unit.manage' (record_type organization for the move to the top level). business_unit.update count = 4, exactly the successful moves and renames. The direct mth_app UPDATE failed: 'business unit ... cannot be placed under its own descendant' (psql exit 1). Closure self-cycles = 0. Outbox transformation.created 7/7 published. The worker exits 0 on SIGTERM, the API stays alive, and /readyz answers 200 ready. api.log has 0 error or fatal lines.

checks_run.procedure: A second API instance with RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=20, same database. Two synthetic users sign in from the same IP. The office user sends 15 normal requests. Then 40 requests come with freshly fabricated session cookies, followed by one anonymous request. Afterwards, check that both validated users are still served and that /readyz is exempt
checks_run.environment: Node v22.22.2, API :3001 with RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=20 and AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000, PostgreSQL 16.13 disposable
checks_run.expected: normal user traffic is served; forged cookies share the IP bucket and get 429 problem+json; validated users keep their own subject buckets; /readyz is never limited
checks_run.actual: SUMMARY pass=7 fail=0. 15 of 15 legitimate requests returned 200. The forged-cookie flood gave {401:20, 429:20}, and the 429 was application/problem+json code rate_limited. The anonymous request from the same IP got 429. dev.office and dev.lead still got 200 and 200 after the flood. /readyz returned 200. Ordinary users keep working under the new keying, and users behind a shared IP are not throttled by a forged-cookie flood.

summary: PASS on candidate sha256:e6979e12… (source 485e91f). All three Low findings I raised in round 1 are verified fixed: F-DG1-001 (the views are documented and match the migrated schema), F-DG1-002 (the clean-start guide states 'currently 9: 0001-0009', matching 'applied 9 migration(s)') and F-DG1-003 (the REQ-S16-001 note cites stable candidate facts, and the worker-stop claim was re-proven live). The round-2 product change does not break domain behaviour. BU cycles are refused with 422 by the API, and by the 0009 trigger at the database. Moves need business_unit.manage on the destination, with 403 refusals audited. The new rate-limit keying serves ordinary users while throttling forged-cookie floods per IP. The cycle refusal is shown in Arabic RTL and English LTR. No regression: the close rule is still 422 under the G6 product gate (never DG7); scoped access, CSRF, If-Match, cursor pagination, provisional branding, bundled fonts, no CDN, and Asia/Riyadh and SAR defaults are unchanged. Every required check ran and passed on Node 22 and Node 24 (326 unit tests each, 209 integration tests). No new findings.
